newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-MOYA BATTLES INTO OPEN SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MOYA BATTLES INTO OPEN SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Unseeded Spaniard Carlos Moya blasted his way into the Australian Open semifinals on Tuesday, beating 14th seeded compatriot Felix Mantilla in four sets.
Moya, the event's giant-killer and pin-up after beating defending champion Boris Becker in the first round, has cut a swathe through the men's draw.
Showing increasing confidence, Moya put friendship to one side to dispose of Mantilla 7-5 6-2 6-7 6-2 in two hours and 29 minutes.
Moya, 20, and the 22-year-old Mantilla are training partners in the former Olympic city of Barcelona.
Known as a baseliner, Moya pushed up to the net throughout the match, volleying well and producing delicate sliced drop shots to which Mantilla could not respond.
Mantilla mounted a fight-back in the third set, winning a tie-break 7-5, but Moya was back in control in the fourth set.
Moya is the first Spanish man to reach the semifinals of the Australian grand slam since Andres Gimeno, runner-up in 1969.
The match was played on centre court, but with none of the heat problems of recent days.
Tournament officials decided on Tuesday to close the retractable stadium roof and turn on the air conditioning, effectively making the Open an indoor tournament for the day.
